title: WPPIL/35/2022 of RAJENDRA SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No. 35 of 2022
Rajendra Singh .................Petitioner.

-Versus-State of Uttarakhand
and others. .........Respondents.
Present:
Shri Abhijay Negi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Shri B.S. Negi, learned counsel for the respondent no. 3.
Shri Aditya Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the respondent no. 4.
Date of hearing and judgment: April 27, 2022
Coram:
Sri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, ACJ.
Sri Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Court has passed
following Judgment (Per : Sri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, ACJ)
1. In this petition, the petitioner, who is an army veteran, has
prayed to issue a writ in the nature of Mandamus commanding
the respondents to establish the dumping yard in an alternative
location then the proposed location at Khasra No. 424 in Gairsain.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner drew attention of this
Court to the provisions of the Solid Waste Management Rules,
2016 issued by the Union of India especially to Schedule I passed
under Rule 15 (w), (zi), 16 (1) (b) (e), 16 (4) of the aforesaid Rules.
In Entry A, criteria for site selection has been mentioned. The sub
Clause (vii) provides that establishment of solid waste site shall
be guided by the following factors:
"(vii) The landfill site shall be 100 meter away from river,
200 meter from a pond, 200 meter from Highways,
Habitations, Public Parks and water supply wells and 20 km

2
away from Airports or Airbase. However in a special case,
landfill site may be set up within a distance of 10 and 20 km
away from the Airport/Airbase after obtaining no objection
certificate from the civil aviation authority/ Air Force as the
case may be. The Landfill site shall not be permitted within
the flood plains as recorded for the last 100 years, zone of
coastal regulation, wetland, Critical habitat areas, sensitive
eco-fragile areas."
3. In that view of the matter, learned counsel for the parties
submit that the matter can be looked into by the District
Magistrate, Chamoli, who can take a call on it.
4. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of by giving
liberty to the petitioner to file a copy of the brief along with
additional affidavit and copy of this order within ten days before
the learned District Magistrate, Chamoli. On such an event, the
learned District Magistrate, Chamoli shall consider the writ
petition as representation and after affording the opportunity of
hearing to the petitioner and respondent nos. 3 and 4, and also
making measurement of the distance from the aforesaid site and
river, pond, highway etc. as referred to above in the provisions
quoted (supra), shall decide the representation by reasoned and
speaking order within 45 days therefrom. We have not passed
any interim order in this petition, in view of the fact that tender
has already been cancelled.
 (Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra)
 Acting Chief Justice.
SKS
